startupCost.note: NatronRenderer 2.4.4 live: --version cold start 11/10/10 ms (mean 10, 3 runs; exits 1 after printing — quirk of the binary, not a failure). Structural pipeline measured: open 1.3ms, exportOtio 1.3ms.

modeComparison.determinism: deterministic generated Python script (Read→Transform→Merge→Write graph) per revision; render determinism verified live on 2.4.4 (script executes and registers the declared output)
modeComparison.sandboxability: high — NatronRenderer is the documented headless binary; cwd-scoped; no GUI
modeComparison.errorSurfacing: exit code + stdout/stderr captured; Python exceptions inside the script appear in stderr and fail the job
modeComparison.artifactFidelity: layer-stack model (not timeline-oriented): record placement beyond the composite stack is dropped, transform x/y/scale/rotation map to the Transform node — declared in codec fidelity notes

modeComparison.note: Natron's Python API only runs inside the Natron process; no out-of-process embedding exists
Natron's Python host could expose an MCP server, but that is a Natron-side plugin project — out of scope
compositing render farms are the natural shape; the adapter ports are the seam

liveConformance: live-verified (NatronRenderer 2.4.4, W11/W12): composite render scenario passes in editor-live.test.ts (suite 48/48); plugin ids are fr.inria.openfx.ReadFFmpeg / net.sf.openfx.TransformPlugin / net.sf.openfx.MergePlugin / fr.inria.openfx.WriteFFmpeg — the legacy fr.inria.natron.* ids return None from createNode on 2.4.4
caveats: createNode ids and the WriteFFmpeg param surface (format/codec/fps, enumerated live via getParams()) are confirmed against the 2.4.4 binary; leaving experimental maturity is a TL decision
